newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Huarte to sell repurchased shares.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Huarte to sell repurchased shares.

text.p: Spanish construction firm Huarte said on Tuesday that it was planning to sell shares it repurchased representing 8.51 percent of its capital.

"Considering the strong demand for Huarte shares and given that Huarte is in possession of 8.51 percent in the form of bought-back shares...Huarte intends to sell these shares," Huarte said in a statement.
The troubled company said the imminent lifting of its suspension of payments and its recent "accordion" operation also supported its decision to sell the shares now.
Huarte suspended payments to suppliers in mid-March after a rescue plan failed.
In October, as part of an accordion operation it reduced its share capital to zero and then increased it to 10.04 billion pesetas.
Spain's stock market commission, the CNMV, said Huarte would sell the shares in the next few days after the lifting of its suspension of payments.
The CNMV said the shares to be sold came at zero cost from a failed economic restructuring deal signed in February with construction company San Jose and other financial backers.
